metadata.description: PointGuard (pgcfo.com) designed privileged-access state for Microsoft Entra, following the Security Provisioning classification and approval model. ADDITIVE, DESIRED STATE ONLY: apart from the delete-protection and database groups (adopted by display name, user decision) and the emergency group (adopted if it exists), the template references no existing group and declares no target-side members or owners list anywhere (those are authoritative and prune even in Incremental mode); every membership it declares is a principal-side, ensure-only edge. CLASSIFICATION: every directory role in roleCatalog carries one classification (excluded, controlPlane, privileged, operational, readOnly) from the Security Provisioning classifier, with one documented override (Global Reader to readOnly); everything else derives from classificationPolicy. Excluded roles (Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator) are held permanently by the RMAU-protected 'Emergency Access - GA-PRA' group only. Control-plane roles are held by nobody; their directory-role PIM policy locks them down behind approval by 'Security - Tenant Approvers' (permanent eligibility and permanent active assignment allowed, user decision). Privileged, operational and read-only roles each get one role group ('Security - <role name>'); how the group holds its role follows Security Provisioning and is data (roleAssignment in classificationPolicy): read-only roles are held permanently (active), privileged and operational roles through a no-expiry PIM eligibility of the group, which the group's members (active members through the access package) activate under the role's directory-role activation policy. Operational policies allow permanent eligibility and permanent active assignment (user decision). PER-SCOPE ACCESS: for each scope in accessScopes the template creates one approver group ('Security - Approvers - <Env>') and one access group per role set in scopeRoleSets ('Security - Privileged Access - <Env>', 'Security - Operational Access - <Env>', 'Security - Read-Only Access - <Env>'; <Env> is the title-cased scope key); ARM assigns the Azure roles to the access groups from the accessGroups output. uniqueNames (pg-..., security-entraroles-...) are the stable keys. Every repeated object is a copy loop over the data, so adding a scope or a role is a parameter change. ACCESS PACKAGES: two catalogs created by the template, 'M365 Catalog' (the role groups' packages) and 'Default Catalog' (the packages of the access groups, approver groups, 'Security - Tenant Approvers', delete-protection groups and database groups). Every packaged group has one access package granting active Member (no Entra ID Governance licence, so no Eligible Member), with an assignment policy 'Approval by <approver group>' declared here: access groups, delete-protection groups and database groups are approved by their scope's approver group, role groups and approver groups by 'Security - Tenant Approvers'; access and role group assignments expire after packageDays, approver groups after 90 days, delete-protection and database groups after 365 days. PIM: every group PIM policy (role groups, access groups, delete-protection groups) opts in to onboarding, naming the template's own disabled account pim-onboarding@<tenant domain> (created here, password generated by EARM and written only to the secure outputs file) for a one-hour member eligibility that EARM removes in the same run, so the policies apply on the first deploy. Conditional Access: four new policies declared enabled (the registration policy covers 'Security - Tenant Approvers', every scope approver group and every role group); a deploy without --allow-ca-enforce creates them report-only and leaves an existing policy's live state alone. Authentication methods: optional CBA-as-MFA only. NOT in this template: other existing groups and their memberships, the baseline Conditional Access policies, access reviews, Azure RBAC/Azure PIM, and every REMOVAL of existing access. Needs Entra ID P2, EARM main at 455cb1e or later, and a delegated Global Administrator (or Privileged Role Administrator + User Administrator + Conditional Access Administrator + Authentication Policy Administrator + Identity Governance Administrator) run: adding role-assignable groups to a catalog needs Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator. See entra/README.md and entra/DECISIONS.md.

userPrincipalNames of the EXISTING break-glass users (breakglass@pgcfo.com and Gnarwhal@pgcfo.com). Each is declared as a users resource with edge properties only (memberOf the emergency group, 'Security - Tenant Approvers' and every scope approver group; administrativeUnits the 'Emergency Access' AU): ensure-only, so EARM adds those edges and never removes a membership or changes the profile. A UPN that does not exist is planned as a user create without displayName, which EARM refuses, so no account is ever created from a typo. Every break-glass user is excluded from the four new Conditional Access policies. The domain of the FIRST entry is also the tenant domain of the PIM onboarding account the template creates (pim-onboarding@<domain>), so list a member account of a verified domain first.

The per-subscription access scopes, from the Security Provisioning preflight. key: lower-case, part of every group uniqueName of the scope (pg-<key>-...); NEVER change it after the first deploy (a new key creates new groups and packages, the old ones stay). The key, title-cased (dev -> Dev), is also the <Env> of every group and package display name of the scope ('Security - Privileged Access - Dev', package 'Privileged Access - Dev'), so a new key also means new package names. name: friendly name used in the group descriptions only. tier: sandbox, nonProduction or production; picks the PIM settings and the access-package expiry of the scope's access groups. subscriptionName / subscriptionId: passed through to the outputs for the ARM side. Adding or removing a scope is a parameter change only; every scopeKey of deleteProtectionGroups and databaseEnvironments must be listed here.

Which role groups (and their PIM policies and access packages) to build: the roleCatalog keys of the roles whose classification gives them a role group (privileged, operational, read-only). Default = all 18. Excluded and control-plane roles never get a group.
Bind certificate-based authentication's default mode to multi-factor (Set-PhishingResistantAuth.ps1 -ConfigureCba). Off by default, as in the script.

catalogs.name: [variables('defaultCatalog')]
catalogs.description: PointGuard access: membership of the per-subscription access groups, the per-subscription approver groups, the tenant approvers, the delete-protection groups and the database groups.

catalogs.name: [variables('m365Catalog')]
catalogs.description: PointGuard Microsoft 365 and Entra directory roles: membership of the directory role groups.

excluded.label: excluded
excluded.summary: Break-glass only: held permanently by the emergency access group, reachable no other way, no PIM policy and no access package.

controlPlane.label: control plane
controlPlane.summary: Can grant or alter privilege held by others. Held by nobody and given no group: the directory-role policy locks the role down so a hand-made eligibility still needs tenant approval to activate. Permanent eligibility and permanent active assignment are allowed (user decision: no expiry required).

privileged.label: privileged
privileged.summary: Carries Microsoft's isPrivileged flag. Never held standing (Security Provisioning): the role group is ELIGIBLE for the role, with no expiry, and its members activate the role through the directory-role PIM policy (these activation settings). Membership of the role group through an access package approved by the tenant approvers, expiring after packageDays.

operational.label: operational
operational.summary: Administers a service or a configuration with no privileged flag (the catch-all). No persona holds it standing in the Security Provisioning access matrix: the role group is ELIGIBLE for the role, with no expiry, and its members activate the role through the directory-role PIM policy. Permanent eligibility and permanent active assignment are allowed (user decision: no expiry required). Membership of the role group through an access package expiring after packageDays.

readOnly.label: read-only
readOnly.summary: Reads only. The role group holds the role permanently (active), the one class Security Provisioning lets a persona hold standing in the directory. Membership of the role group through an access package; standing active membership is allowed (gating a reader adds friction, not safety).

classificationOverride.reason: Microsoft tags it isPrivileged, which is why the classifier places it in privileged. 99 of its 103 actions are pure reads and it can grant nothing; PointGuard treats it as the read-only role it behaves like, so it can be held standing.
classificationOverride.acceptedRisk: It reads BitLocker recovery keys (microsoft.directory/bitlockerKeys/key/read) and device local administrator credentials (microsoft.directory/deviceLocalCredentials/standard/read) tenant-wide. Standing Global Reader means standing access to both, with no activation record when either is retrieved.

properties.description: Approves privileged access at the tenant scope: the control-plane directory-role lock-down policies and the access packages of the role groups, the scope approver groups and this group. Both break-glass accounts are members as approvers of last resort. Needs at least two day-to-day members so peers can approve each other.

Break-glass accounts are permanent members (recovery path); security-owners and security-uat-contributor are PIM-eligible and must activate with MFA + approval.

DELETE PROTECTION for the production subscription. The ONLY principal excluded from the '*/delete' deny assignment at that scope, so membership is what permits any delete there. Break-glass accounts are permanent members (recovery path); security-owners and security-prd-contributor are PIM-eligible and must activate with MFA + approval.

resources.name: [variables('emergencyGroup')]
resources.comments: Emergency access. Its permanent roles are the roleCatalog entries classified 'excluded' (Global Administrator, Privileged Role Administrator), held through directoryRoles (role assignments, not PIM: objects in an RMAU cannot be PIM-governed). Create-if-missing, modify-if-present: EARM looks the group up by uniqueName; if none has it, it adopts the single existing group with exactly this displayName and no uniqueName, otherwise it creates it. No members list: the break-glass users join through their own ensure-only memberOf edges. An adopted group keeps any member it already has: review its members before the run.

properties.description: Break-glass only. Sole holder of Global Administrator and Privileged Role Administrator (permanent). Protected by the 'Emergency Access' restricted management AU. Every member sign-in must alert.

resources.name: [variables('emergencyAu')]
resources.comments: Emergency-access RMAU. isMemberManagementRestricted is fixed at creation. No members list: the break-glass users and the emergency group join through their own ensure-only administrativeUnits edges; after that only Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator can change them, so run delegated as GA/PRA.

properties.description: Restricted management: the break-glass accounts and the Emergency Access - GA-PRA group

resources.name: [parameters('breakGlassUserPrincipalNames')[copyIndex()]]
resources.comments: The EXISTING break-glass accounts, adopted by userPrincipalName with edge properties ONLY (principal-side, ensure-only: added when missing, never removed; no profile property, so the account is never changed). memberOf is a property copy over breakGlassGroups: the emergency group, 'Security - Tenant Approvers' and every scope approver group (approvers of last resort through membership, so the first request always has somebody able to approve it). The accounts must already exist.

resources.name: [variables('pimOnboardingAccount')]
resources.comments: The PIM onboarding account, created by the template (a new object, so an additive create): pim-onboarding@<tenant domain>, the domain taken from the first break-glass userPrincipalName. DISABLED and never signs in: its only use is the one-hour member eligibility every group PIM policy's onboarding opt-in requests for a group PIM for Groups has not onboarded yet, which EARM removes again in the same run. No password is declared: EARM generates a random one at creation and writes it only to the --secure-outputs-file (oneTimeSecrets); it is never in the template, the parameters or the what-if. accountEnabled is declared, so a later deploy disables the account again if somebody enables it.

resources.name: [variables('tenantApprovers').uniqueName]
resources.comments: The single approver group of the tenant scope: approves the control-plane lock-down policies and the access packages of the role groups, the scope approver groups and itself. No members list (additive): the break-glass accounts join through their own memberOf edges, people through its access package. Role-assignable (create-only) so that only Global Administrator / Privileged Role Administrator can change who approves.

resources.name: [variables('approverGroups')[copyIndex()].uniqueName]
resources.comments: One role-assignable approver group per scope in accessScopes; it approves that scope's access packages. No members list; no PIM policy (nobody activates membership of an approver group).

resources.name: [variables('accessGroups')[copyIndex()].uniqueName]
resources.comments: One role-assignable access group per scope and role set: one loop over the flattened accessScopes x scopeRoleSets array. Holds Azure roles only (assigned by the ARM side from the accessGroups output); role-assignable by user decision, the only protection from tenant-wide Groups Administrator. No members list.

resources.name: [variables('roleGroups')[copyIndex()].uniqueName]
resources.comments: One role-assignable group per role classified privileged, operational or read-only and listed in enabledRoleKeys. The classification's roleAssignment decides how the group holds its role: read-only roles PERMANENTLY (directoryRoles edge, active, no expiry); privileged and operational roles through a PIM eligibility of the group (roleEligibilities loop, no expiry), so members activate the role under its directory-role policy and the group declares no directoryRoles edge. No members list. Display name 'Security - <role name>' (user decision), uniqueName security-entraroles-<key> (stable). EARM's displayName fallback would adopt an existing group with the same displayName and no uniqueName: no known existing or planned group carries these names, and the first what-if must show Create for every one.

resources.name: [variables('adoptedGroups')[copyIndex()].uniqueName]
resources.comments: The EXISTING delete-protection groups ('Security - Delete Protection - Shared' / 'Uat' / 'Prd', from Set-DeleteProtection.ps1) and database groups ('db-<env>-reader' / 'writer' / 'owner', from Set-EnvironmentSecurityGroups.ps1), adopted by their exact displayName (user decision): EARM stamps a uniqueName once and creates a group only where none has that name. Only the properties the scripts set are declared; no members or owners list. The deny assignments and the database roles bind to these groups by object id (protectionGroups and databaseGroups outputs). Each also gets an access package in 'Default Catalog' (user decision): Member, approved by the scope's approver group, expiring after protectedMembershipDays (365).

resources.name: [variables('groupPimPolicies')[copyIndex()].policyName]
resources.comments: The PIM for Groups MEMBER policy of every role group (from its classification) and every access group (from scopeAccessPolicy by role set and scope tier): activation duration, MFA / justification / ticketing, NO approval (approval lives on the access package), maximum active-membership duration and eligibility expiry. Kept on the role groups whose role is eligible too: Security Provisioning declares a member policy for every directory class group, and it governs any PIM membership made outside the access packages. Onboarding opt-in: a group PIM for Groups has not onboarded yet is onboarded in the same run through a one-hour member eligibility of the template's disabled onboarding account, which EARM removes again (PimOnboardingEligibilityNotRemoved if the removal fails).

resources.name: [guid('pg-delete-protection-policy', variables('deleteProtectionGroups')[copyIndex()].scopeKey, 'member')]
resources.comments: The PIM for Groups MEMBER policy of each delete-protection group, copied rule for rule from Set-DeleteProtection.ps1 / Set-GroupPimPolicy (_GroupPim.ps1): permanent eligibility allowed (cap P365D for time-bound ones), activation 8 hours, MFA + justification, approval by the delete-protection group ITSELF (the script default; its break-glass members are the standing approvers), 1 day timeout, no escalation. Expiration_Admin_Assignment is not declared because the script does not write it. The existing groups are already onboarded by the script's eligibilities, so the onboarding opt-in only acts on a group EARM had to create.

resources.name: [guid('pg-role-policy', variables('directoryRolePolicies')[copyIndex()].templateId)]
resources.comments: Directory-role PIM policies, tenant-wide for each role: they change the rules for EVERY principal eligible for the role, including principals eligible today. Removes no live eligibility or assignment. Two kinds, one loop over directoryRolePolicies. LOCK-DOWN (each control-plane role, held by nobody, no group): approval by Security - Tenant Approvers, 1 hour activation, MFA + justification + ticketing, permanent eligibility and permanent active assignment allowed (user decision); always applied (user decision: no switch). ACTIVATION (each privileged or operational role whose role group is eligible for it): the activation gates of the classification (hours, MFA, justification, ticketing for privileged; no approval, which lives on the access package), active assignments expire after the classification's active maximum (operational: permanent allowed, user decision), and permanent eligibility is ALLOWED so the role group's no-expiry eligibility is accepted (the group's eligibility is infrastructure, as Security Provisioning's standing-assignment carve-out treats a group's standing role). EARM applies each policy before the eligibility request of the same role.

resources.name: [guid('pg-role-eligibility', variables('eligibleRoleGroups')[copyIndex()].roleKey)]
resources.comments: The PIM eligibility of each role group whose classification's roleAssignment is eligible (privileged and operational) for its directory role at the tenant ('/'), with no expiry (no scheduleInfo). Members of the group, who are active members through the access package, activate the role themselves under the role's activation policy. Additive: a new eligibility for a new group; nothing else is touched.

properties.justification: [format('PointGuard role group for {0}: eligible, members activate the role through PIM', variables('eligibleRoleGroups')[copyIndex()].roleName)]

resources.name: [variables('catalogs')[copyIndex()].name]
resources.comments: The two catalogs, created by the template (user decision; neither exists yet): 'M365 Catalog' holds the packages of the directory role groups, 'Default Catalog' every other package (access groups, scope approver groups, the tenant approvers, delete-protection groups, database groups). Each package names its catalog (package.catalog). Created published and not externally visible. A catalog is found by display name: an existing catalog with one of these names would be adopted, so the first what-if must show Create.

resources.name: [guid(variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.catalog, variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].uniqueName)]
resources.comments: Every group that gets an access package added to its package's catalog: the role groups to 'M365 Catalog'; the access groups, scope approver groups, the tenant approvers, delete-protection groups and database groups to 'Default Catalog'. The role groups, access groups and approver groups are role-assignable, so this needs a delegated Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator run (CatalogResourceAccessDenied otherwise); the delete-protection and database groups are not role-assignable.

resources.name: [variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.name]
resources.comments: One access package per packaged group, in the catalog its entry names. The name is the package's identity and must stay unique in the tenant: role groups use the role name, access groups '<Role set> Access - <Env>', approver groups 'Approvers - <Env>', the tenant approvers 'Tenant Approvers', delete-protection groups 'DeleteProtection - <Env>', database groups 'Database <Tier> - <Env>'.

properties.description: [format('Membership of {0}, approved by {1}; it ends after {2} days.', variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].properties.displayName, variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.approverName, variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.days)]

resources.name: [guid(variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.name, 'Member')]
resources.comments: Each package grants active Member of its group (user decision: no Entra ID Governance licence, so no Eligible Member; the groups hold the roles).

resources.name: [format('{0}/Approval by {1}', variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.name, variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.approverName)]
resources.comments: The assignment policy of each package (people decide the settings; the template carries them): every member user may request, one approval stage by the package's approver group with justification from both sides, denied after 14 days without a decision, and the assignment expires after package.days: access and role groups the packageDays of their policy, approver groups approverMembershipDays, delete-protection and database groups protectedMembershipDays (approved by the scope's approver group). The name is 'Approval by <approver group display name>'.

properties.description: [format('Member users request it; {0} approve; it ends after {1} days.', variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.approverName, variables('packagedGroups')[copyIndex()].package.days)]

resources.name: [variables('pimElevationAuthenticationContextId')]
resources.comments: The id (c1) is a design constant: the 'Phishing-resistant MFA for PIM elevation' policy (and later the PIM rules) refer to it, so it must stay stable once deployed, and it must be unused in the tenant before the first deploy.

properties.description: For PIM activation of the privileged classification once PIM rules move from MFA to authentication context (enforced by the 'Phishing-resistant MFA for PIM elevation' policy). No PIM rule requests it yet.
Phishing-resistant: elevated or becoming elevated. Windows Hello for Business or FIDO2 passkey.

resources.name: [variables('passwordlessStrength')]
resources.comments: Passwordless strength from the design section 'Tiered authentication strengths'. No policy in this template uses it yet.

properties.description: Passwordless: ordinary sign-in. Authenticator passwordless (not phishing-resistant, accepted) or any phishing-resistant method.
Bootstrap for registering security info: a Temporary Access Pass, or an existing phishing-resistant method.

resources.name: Phishing-resistant MFA for PIM elevation
resources.comments: Targets the PIM authentication context ONLY (a CA policy must not combine includeApplications with an authentication context). No PIM rule requests the context yet; enforce this BEFORE any PIM rule is switched from MFA to the authentication context. Every Conditional Access policy excludes the break-glass users through a property copy.

resources.name: Phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles
resources.comments: Covers the roles whose classification sets requiresPhishingResistantSignIn (excluded, control plane, privileged). Split from the PIM elevation policy because it needs includeApplications All.

resources.name: Session controls for privileged roles
resources.comments: Same role list as 'Phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles'. Sign-in frequency 8 hours (the longest activation window of any classification); persistent browser never (requires All cloud apps).

resources.name: Strong method or TAP to register security info
resources.comments: Registration bootstrap from the design section 'Tiered authentication strengths'. Scoped, not all users: Security - Tenant Approvers, every scope approver group and every role group (user decision; one property copy over registrationGroups) plus active holders of the roles that require phishing-resistant sign-in. User action only (no includeApplications). This template does NOT configure the Temporary Access Pass method; the TAP combination only works while TAP is enabled in the tenant by other means.

resources.name: x509Certificate
resources.comments: CBA default binding multi-factor; existing rules kept (rules not declared).

metadata.description: One entry per scope: { scopeKey, subscriptionId, uniqueName, groupId }.

One entry per scope and role set: { scopeKey, subscriptionId, roleSetKey (privileged, operational, readOnly), uniqueName, groupId }. ARM assigns each role set's Azure roles at the subscription to groupId.
One entry per delete-protection group: { scopeKey, subscriptionId, uniqueName, groupId }. groupId is the principal the scope's '*/delete' deny assignment excludes.
One entry per database group: { scopeKey, subscriptionId, tier (reader, writer, owner), uniqueName, groupId }. The database roles (and, for owner, the Postgres Entra administrator) bind to groupId.
